title.en: Meaning, nature and objectives of financial statements

hook.en: Every year a listed company publishes an annual report. At its heart are two *statements* that tell shareholders what the company owns, owes and earned.
hook.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ವರ್ಷ ಕಂಪನಿ ವಾರ್ಷಿಕ ವರದಿ ಪ್ರಕಟಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಅದರ ಹೃದಯಭಾಗದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಎರಡು ತಃಖ್ತೆಗಳು ಕಂಪನಿಯ ಆಸ್ತಿ, ಸಾಲ ಮತ್ತು ಗಳಿಕೆಯನ್ನು ತಿಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

say.en: Every year a listed company publishes an annual report. At its heart are two statements that tell shareholders what the company owns, owes and earned. In this lesson: Define financial statements.
Explain their nature.
List their objectives.

body.en: *Financial statements* are the end products of the accounting process: the Balance Sheet (position on a date) and the Statement of Profit and Loss (performance for a period), with notes to accounts and, where applicable, a Cash Flow Statement. They are a mix of recorded facts, accounting conventions, postulates and personal judgements.
body.kn: ಹಣಕಾಸು ತಃಖ್ತೆಗಳು ಲೆಕ್ಕಪತ್ರ ಪ್ರಕ್ರಿಯೆಯ ಅಂತಿಮ ಫಲ: ಆಸ್ತಿ-ಜವಾಬ್ದಾರಿ ತಃಖ್ತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಲಾಭ ನಷ್ಟದ ತಃಖ್ತೆ. ಇವು ದಾಖಲಿತ ಸತ್ಯಾಂಶಗಳು, ಸಂಪ್ರದಾಯಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ವೈಯಕ್ತಿಕ ತೀರ್ಮಾನಗಳ ಮಿಶ್ರಣ.

title.en: A company's statement of profit and loss

narration.en: Schedule III sets the order: revenue from operations and other income, less expenses, gives profit before tax; tax expense is deducted to give the profit for the period, which goes to the balance sheet under reserves and surplus. Raise the tax rate from 22% to 30%. What happens to profit for the year? Make expenses exceed revenue. Is any tax charged?
narration.kn: ಅನುಸೂಚಿ III ಕ್ರಮ ನಿಗದಿಪಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ: ಕಾರ್ಯಾಚರಣೆ ಆದಾಯ ಮತ್ತು ಇತರ ಆದಾಯದಿಂದ ವೆಚ್ಚ ಕಳೆದರೆ ತೆರಿಗೆ ಮೊದಲ ಲಾಭ; ತೆರಿಗೆ ಕಳೆದರೆ ಅವಧಿಯ ಲಾಭ, ಅದು ಆಸ್ತಿ-ಹೊಣೆ ಪಟ್ಟಿಯ ಮೀಸಲು ಮತ್ತು ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿಗೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತದೆ. ತೆರಿಗೆ ದರವನ್ನು 22%ರಿಂದ 30%ಕ್ಕೆ ಏರಿಸಿ. ವರ್ಷದ ಲಾಭ ಏನಾಗುತ್ತದೆ? ವೆಚ್ಚ ಆದಾಯಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾಗಲಿ. ತೆರಿಗೆ ಉಂಟೇ?

title.en: On the board: What financial statements are

narration.en: A company's financial statements are a set: two main statements, notes and a cash flow statement.

say.en: A company's financial statements are a set: two main statements, notes and a cash flow statement.
They are made of four ingredients: recorded facts, conventions, postulates and personal judgements.
Cash counted is a recorded fact; inventory at cost or lower market price is a convention; choosing the depreciation method is a judgement.

problem.en: Classify each fact as a recorded fact, a convention, or a personal judgement: (a) cash in hand ₹25,000; (b) inventory valued at cost or net realisable value, whichever is lower; (c) machinery depreciated by the written down value method at 15%.

steps.en: (a) Cash in hand is counted and recorded: a recorded fact.
(b) Valuing inventory at the lower of cost or NRV follows the convention of conservatism (prudence).
(c) Choosing WDV and the rate of 15% is a personal judgement of management.

narration.en: Let us work this out together, step by step.

say.en: Let us work this out together, step by step. Classify each fact as a recorded fact, a convention, or a personal judgement: a cash in hand 25,000 rupees; b inventory valued at cost or net realisable value, whichever is lower; c machinery depreciated by the written down value method at 15 percent.
a Cash in hand is counted and recorded: a recorded fact.
b Valuing inventory at the lower of cost or NRV follows the convention of conservatism prudence.
c Choosing WDV and the rate of 15 percent is a personal judgement of management.
So the answer is a recorded fact; b convention; c personal judgement.
